exercises.title: Beyond RD 1 — requirements as the hub
exercises.problemHtml:
Figure 19-1: requirements are the hub — they drive project planning, design, coding and testing. Every downstream activity traces back to them, which is why a requirement defect ripples so widely. Requirements effort is spread differently by life cycle: a sequential project front-loads it; an iterative or incremental project spreads it across iterations.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Beyond RD 2 — size measures from requirements
exercises.problemHtml:
Estimating size and effort from requirements can use: the number of individually testable requirements; function points; story points or use case points; the number, type and complexity of UI elements; or estimated lines of code per requirement. Name the measure each team uses.

exercises.title: Beyond RD 3 — from size to effort and schedule
exercises.problemHtml:
Effective scheduling needs an estimated product size, the team’s known productivity from history, and the effort for every task. Write function plan(size, hoursPerUnit, teamHoursPerWeek, contingencyPct) that returns { effortHours, weeks }: effort = size × hoursPerUnit, increased by contingencyPct percent and rounded up to a whole hour; weeks = effort ÷ team hours per week, rounded up. Then set CLINIC_PLAN for ClinicCare: 140 testable requirements, 6.5 hours each, a team of 4 people × 30 productive hours per week, 20% contingency.

Requirements

  • plan(100, 5, 120, 10) ⇒ { effortHours: 550, weeks: 5 }.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Viết plan(size, hoursPerUnit, teamHoursPerWeek, contingencyPct) trả { effortHours, weeks } (làm tròn lên), rồi CLINIC_PLAN cho ClinicCare.

Yêu cầu

  • plan(100, 5, 120, 10) ⇒ { effortHours: 550, weeks: 5 }.

exercises.title: Beyond RD 4 — plans that follow the requirements
exercises.problemHtml:
Base plans on requirements and refine them as requirements become clearer; early estimates from fuzzy requirements are uncertain. If planning shows the full feature set cannot fit the available time and resources, reduce scope or stage the releases — on agile, scope is adjusted to the time-boxes.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
